entries.question: What capabilities and evidence establish useful robotic autonomy?

entries.question: How should robots recover from localization or actuation failure?

entries.question: How can we calculate a manipulator's forward kinematics and Jacobian?
aliases: Can you compute forward kinematics and a robot arm's Jacobian from its joint model?
entries.success_criterion: Given joint transforms and configuration, calculate end-effector pose and velocity Jacobian, and check against a direct transform or finite difference.

entries.question: How can we update a robot's state belief using a sensor observation?
aliases: Can you perform one Bayesian sensor update for a robot state estimate?
entries.success_criterion: Given a prior and observation model, calculate a normalized posterior and test how it changes when the evidence is uninformative.

entries.question: How can we compute the actuator torques needed for a robot's motion?
aliases: How strong do my robot motors need to be?
entries.success_criterion: Given a rigid-link model, joint trajectory and stated external loads, calculate joint torques; check a static or single-joint limiting case and compare against the actuator's limits.

landscape_views.title: How can I build a working autonomous robot?
landscape_views.rationale: Build a mission as a compositional contract, rather than treating any individual algorithm as the robot.

landscape_views.title: How do bodies, joints and motion constraints fit together?
landscape_views.rationale: Distinguish representation, reachable configurations, feasible instantaneous velocities and dynamically achievable motion.

landscape_views.title: How does a robot know where it is and what surrounds it?
landscape_views.rationale: Separate sensor evidence, filter assumptions, localization with a known map and joint inference of poses and map.

landscape_views.title: How do plans become physically valid stable movements?
landscape_views.rationale: Compose collision avoidance, timing, trajectory control, actuator dynamics and contact-mode choice.

landscape_views.title: How does a fixed-wing autonomous mission actually work?
landscape_views.rationale: Air/ground relative physics → trim → estimated flight state → inner loops → guidance/path manager → flight test envelope.

landscape_views.title: How can uncertainty change what a robot should do next?
landscape_views.rationale: From recursive beliefs through alternative inference representations to information-seeking control and exploration.

landscape_views.title: How do robots move, grasp and assemble objects?
landscape_views.rationale: Link joint reachability, spatial force propagation, force closure and compliant interaction.

landscape_views.title: Why does an apparently correct robotics system fail?
landscape_views.rationale: Use mismatched predictions, observability, frame conventions, saturation, false correspondence, contact constraints, timing and recovery as competing explanations.

nodes.question: How can physical machines perceive, reason, move and interact reliably across different bodies and environments?
nodes.why: A planar rover, a manipulator and a fixed-wing aircraft share state, estimation and control abstractions but not all motion constraints or force laws.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Factor any robot into embodiment/actuation, physical state and representations, sensing and inference, goals/planning, feedback/action, contact/world interaction, computation and verification. Interfaces—not book divisions—govern reuse.

nodes.question: How can several moving bodies describe the same physical point without frame confusion?
nodes.why: An orientation convention and direction-of-transform error may appear as controller or sensor malfunction; camera/body versus inertial frame changes projection.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: A pose maps coordinates between reference frames. SE(3) rigid transforms compose; twists carry spatial velocity; aircraft wind/air/body/navigation frames add a critical velocity-frame distinction.

nodes.question: Which shapes, joints and constraints determine the states a robot can reach?
nodes.why: A reachable endpoint may not be reachable by a collision-free, kinematically feasible path; wheel rolling constraints differ from closed-chain loop closure.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Configuration space describes valid mechanism configurations; workspace is the set of attainable task-space positions. Holonomic constraints remove configurations; nonholonomic constraints restrict velocities and paths even when positions remain reachable.

nodes.question: How can joint positions and velocities be mapped to an end-effector pose or vice versa?
nodes.why: The forward problem is not the inverse problem; a Jacobian singularity can lose a direction of motion or amplify rates/forces.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Product of exponentials composes joint screw motions into end-effector pose using a base and tool frame. Jacobians map joint rates to spatial velocity; inverse kinematics solves the reverse, often nonuniquely.

nodes.question: Why can't a wheeled robot or aircraft always travel along a straight line to its goal?
nodes.why: Geometric reachability, instantaneous steerability and dynamic flight feasibility are different conditions.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Rolling wheels impose nonholonomic velocity constraints; fixed-wing aircraft have minimum-speed and turning limits. Feasible paths must respect vehicle-specific motion families, not just collision-free geometry.

nodes.question: What forces and actuator commands actually accelerate a robot?
nodes.why: Kinematic command feasibility does not imply actuator torque, thermal, transmission or contact feasibility.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Mass/inertia, gravity, Coriolis/centrifugal terms and external forces determine motion. Recursive Newton–Euler inverse dynamics propagates link accelerations forward and wrenches/torques backward.

nodes.question: How can an aircraft stay aloft, turn, climb and recover from disturbances?
nodes.why: Ground speed is not airspeed; a controller that tracks course or altitude may fail from stall, saturation or gust despite correct navigation geometry.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Fixed-wing force and moment models aggregate distributed aerodynamic pressure into lift, drag, side forces and moments; the dynamic pressure scales with air density and squared airspeed, while propulsion and wind perturb motion.

nodes.question: How do we turn nonlinear aircraft physics into tractable controllers?
nodes.why: Linear models describe a neighborhood of trim, not the entire flight envelope; heading can evolve during steady-turn trim.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Trim finds steady flight conditions, including equilibrium or relative equilibrium; linearization gives local transfer/state-space models around an operating condition. A coordinated turn may have a changing heading while remaining steady in the appropriate variables.

nodes.question: What does each sensor truly measure—and what can it never observe alone?
nodes.why: An IMU integrates into drift; a monocular image has scale ambiguity; GNSS provides different information from a gyroscope or wheel encoder.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: A measurement model maps hidden state and calibration/noise into sensor observations: camera pixels, range returns, rates, accelerations, pressure and satellite position impose different constraints. Sensor fusion should distinguish observability from noise averaging.

nodes.question: How does a robot keep track of what might be true when observations are noisy?
nodes.why: A posterior is not just a filtered sensor readout. Wrong independence assumptions, missed dynamics or incorrect likelihoods can yield confident but wrong estimates.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: The recursive Bayes filter predicts a belief using a transition model and corrects it using measurement likelihood; the Markov state and models must include variables needed for conditional independence.

nodes.question: When is a compact mean-and-covariance estimate adequate?
nodes.why: A single Gaussian cannot faithfully encode separated competing pose hypotheses; filter consistency can collapse under wrong nonlinear models.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Kalman filtering is exact for linear Gaussian models; EKF linearizes locally; UKF approximates nonlinear propagation via sigma points; aircraft observers couple high-rate model prediction with lower-rate updates.

nodes.question: How do we represent uncertainty when several explanations remain plausible?
nodes.why: Resampling can impoverish hypotheses; a Gaussian filter may mask multimodality; dense high-dimensional particle spaces are costly.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Particle filters represent a belief by weighted samples and resample them after observations. They support multimodality/nonlinear transformations but depend on a viable proposal distribution and enough particle diversity.

nodes.question: What happens if the robot mistakes one object or place for another?
nodes.why: A mathematically accurate backend cannot recover a correct map from arbitrary false correspondences.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Data association decides which observations correspond to landmarks and previous encounters. Wrong correspondence can enforce false graph constraints and corrupt a map; multiple hypotheses or gated matching control the ambiguity.

nodes.why: Pose tracking with a known initial pose is easier than global localization; failure recovery needs explicit hypothesis renewal.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Localization fuses a motion model with map-conditioned measurements. EKF localization often tracks local uncertainty; grid/Monte Carlo localization supports global or multimodal pose beliefs and kidnapped-robot recovery.

nodes.question: How can raw range returns become a map rather than an accumulation of hits?
nodes.why: Unknown cells, free space and obstacles are not synonyms; mapping with assumed known poses differs from simultaneous pose-and-map inference.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Occupancy grids represent spatial cells' occupancy probabilities; inverse sensor models update traversed/free/occupied cells, with log-odds useful for repeated observations. Pose uncertainty and scan model mismatch propagate into map errors.

nodes.question: How can a machine map a place if it cannot yet know precisely where it is?
nodes.why: Map error and localization error feed each other; mapping with known poses is a simpler different problem.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: SLAM couples uncertain robot trajectory and landmark/map state; pose drift and landmark ambiguity require joint inference, loop closure and appropriate representation. The problem is not solved by alternating naive odometry and drawing walls.

nodes.mechanism_explanation: FastSLAM uses a particle representation of robot paths while estimating features independently conditioned on each path; known paths d-separate the map features. This is a probabilistic factorization, not simply faster code.

nodes.why: A collision-free route executed too quickly may violate actuator limits or contact stability.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: A geometric path specifies positions/configurations, whereas time-scaling assigns velocities and accelerations to meet torque, jerk and safety constraints. For manipulated objects contact constraints also enter.

nodes.question: Why is drawing waypoints insufficient to make an aircraft actually follow them?
nodes.why: Path planning, guidance and inner-loop control are separate contracts; a path can be geometric but violate minimum turn radius.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: A path manager selects feasible lines/orbits and transitions; a guidance law converts cross-track error and geometry into course commands; the autopilot must track those commands under speed, turn and wind limits.

nodes.question: Why might a drone hold its roll well but still fly the wrong course?
nodes.why: A stable slow outer loop cannot overcome a saturated or bandwidth-limited inner loop; fixed-wing lift/control constraints cannot be abstracted away.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Successive loop closure uses faster inner attitude/rate loops to support slower outer course/altitude/airspeed loops; saturation imposes a ceiling on achievable inner-loop performance and therefore downstream loops.

nodes.why: A robot cannot independently dictate both motion and contact force in the same constrained direction; friction cones differ from geometric enclosure.

nodes.question: What if the robot must choose actions before knowing the true state?
nodes.why: Moving toward a goal and moving to disambiguate pose can be competing actions; full POMDP planning scales poorly.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: MDPs optimize actions over known state; POMDPs optimize over belief states where actions can improve both task reward and information. Belief space is itself an evolving decision state.

cross_book_factors.function: Turn raw observations into a position estimate resilient to ambiguous environments
cross_book_factors.operator_chain: MR Ch 3 frame semantics → PR Ch 5 motion model / Ch 6 sensor likelihood → PR Ch 2 Bayes recursion → PR Ch 3 EKF or Ch 4 particle representation → PR Chs 7–8 localization/recovery
cross_book_factors.critical_contract: Coordinate frames, measurement timestamps, covariance or multi-hypothesis belief, failure-recovery strategy
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Teleport in a symmetric environment and measure recovery, false confidence and compute

cross_book_factors.function: Navigate an unknown building without accumulating a hopeless map
cross_book_factors.operator_chain: PR Ch 9 inverse range mapping → PR Chs 10–13 SLAM and loop closure → MR Ch 10 geometry/collision paths → MR Ch 11 controller → PR Ch 17 exploration
cross_book_factors.critical_contract: Map confidence, pose-frame consistency, obstacle margin, recovery policy and update latency
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Inject one false loop closure, one dynamic obstacle and one unknown corridor

cross_book_factors.function: Reach, grasp and move an object without destroying the part or saturating joints
cross_book_factors.operator_chain: MR Chs 2–5 configuration/twists/Jacobian → Ch 6 inverse kinematics → Ch 8 dynamics → Ch 9 timing → Ch 11 force/impedance → Ch 12 grasp
cross_book_factors.critical_contract: Reachability, singularity margin, motor torque, contact force, slip and timing
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Compare free-space versus wall-contact manipulation under one trajectory/controller

cross_book_factors.function: Build a model-based fixed-wing autonomous mission from physics to navigation
cross_book_factors.operator_chain: UAV Chs 2–5 frame/airspeed/forces/trim → Ch 6 cascaded autopilot → Chs 7–8 sensors/estimator → Chs 9–11 guidance/path manager → Chs 12–13 planning/vision
cross_book_factors.critical_contract: Airspeed and stall margin, surface saturation, inner/outer loop bandwidth, wind bias, GPS updates
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Fly a simulated route with crosswind, sensor dropout, actuator saturation and the same logged mission contract

cross_book_factors.function: Decide whether to act or gather information
cross_book_factors.operator_chain: PR Ch 2 belief update → Ch 14 MDP contrast → Ch 15 POMDP → Ch 16 approximation → Ch 17 information gain
cross_book_factors.critical_contract: Reward versus entropy reduction, observation cost, action risk and computation budget
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Two indistinguishable corridors: compare rush-to-goal policy with one sensing detour

cross_book_factors.function: Separate 'where is it' from 'how may it move' from 'what changes motion'
cross_book_factors.operator_chain: MR Chs 2–3 configuration and transforms → MR Chs 4–8 kinematics/dynamics → UAV Chs 3–5 aircraft physical constraints → PR Ch 5 stochastic motion models
cross_book_factors.critical_contract: Type-safe frames, physical units, admissible velocity/acceleration controls, uncertainty and model validity
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Pass the same waypoint plan to a differential rover and fixed-wing aircraft; document incompatible contracts

cross_book_factors.function: Turn a camera detection into world-referenced action
cross_book_factors.operator_chain: MR Ch 3 frame composition → UAV Ch 13 camera/gimbal model / geometric projection → PR Ch 6 observation modeling → UAV Chs 9–10 path following
cross_book_factors.critical_contract: Extrinsic calibration, scale observability, target motion assumptions, latency and course feasibility
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Move camera and target separately, compare geolocation and time-to-collision inferred from projection

cross_book_factors.function: Turn a perfect-model success into a meaningful systems demonstration
cross_book_factors.operator_chain: UAV Ch 1 end-to-end design project → MR Ch 8 motor/friction and Ch 11 control → PR Ch 6 sensor errors / Ch 8 recovery → UAV Ch 6 actuator limits
cross_book_factors.critical_contract: Timing, model discrepancy, calibration, sensor outage, recovery and failure diagnostics
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Run the same mission under ideal, noisy and failing components; compare outcome and traces

cross_book_factors.function: Understand why FastSLAM and multilevel autopilots are both forms of useful decomposition
cross_book_factors.operator_chain: PR Ch 13 conditional independence over features given path → MR Ch 4 products of screw motions for joint chain → UAV Ch 6 fast-inner/slow-outer control hierarchy
cross_book_factors.critical_contract: What is conditioned, composed or approximated; what state/interface must pass between factors
cross_book_factors.discriminator: Remove one factor's assumption (known path, rigid link, or inner-loop bandwidth) and compare collapse behavior

embodiment_matrix.distinctive_constraints: Airspeed-dependent lift, wind, minimum turn radius and no in-place hover

embodiment_matrix.distinctive_constraints: Contact schedule, balance, impacts and many-DOF dynamics

research_boundaries: Not a universal robotics ontology: the three books strongly cover classical geometry, probabilistic mobile robotics and fixed-wing autopilots; advanced legged, multirotor, soft, learning-based and field safety domains require other sources.
Source-section inspection refers to reading relevant extracted source passages, not reproducing calculations, figures or physical experiments.
TOC-derived printed-page anchors are not exact PDF viewer page indices; Kami deep links and precise PDF offsets have not been verified.
State estimation depends on correct model, calibration and time alignment; successful filter math alone does not certify localization.
Flight examples are fixed-wing and instructional; no physical flight safety or regulatory compliance is implied.
Vocabulary links are navigational associations, never evidence of a causal diagnosis.
Structural graph checks test referential consistency, not human usability or real-world competence.
